sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: **Git** is a tool that tracks changes to files over time.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: Git does this too, but with three key differences:↵**Works offline** — No internet needed↵**Full copy on your computer** — Every version, ever↵**No vendor lock-in** — Your data stays yours

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: Here's the powerful part: **Git uses cryptography to make history tamper-proof**.↵Every change gets a unique fingerprint (called a "hash").

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: This fingerprint is calculated from:↵The content you changed↵The fingerprint of the previous change↵Who made the change and when↵This creates a **chain of fingerprints**—just like blockchain.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: If someone tries to alter history (say, delete evidence of who approved a change), the fingerprints no longer match.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: The tampering is **instantly detectable**.↵Confluence and Word can't do this.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: Their logs can be modified by admins.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: Git's history **cannot be silently changed**.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: Git has an even stronger security feature: **commit signing**.↵Every person gets a **personal certificate** (like a digital ID card).

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: When you save a change, Git signs it with your certificate.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: The signature proves: *"This change came from me, and I approve it."*↵**Real-World Analogy:**↵ ↵**Why signing matters:**↵**Prevents impersonation** — Nobody can pretend to be you↵**Legal validity** — Signed commits hold up in court (like a wet signature)↵**Supply chain security** — Know exactly who approved each change↵**Compliance** — Required for some regulated industries↵**What you see in practice:**↵ ↵GitHub and GitLab show a green "Verified" badge on signed commits.

sourceRef.title: Your Documentation Is a Time Bomb: Why 2029 Will Force Your Hand

sentences.text: If someone tries to fake a commit from you, the signature won't match—instantly exposed.
